Article Title: Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family
Article Text:
Inspiring story on parenthood: “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood” – What Andre Agassi and wife Steffi Graf’s parenting journey teaches about raising a family

What did Andre Agassi mean when he said, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood”?

How did becoming a father change Agassi’s view of his own childhood?

How did Steffi Graf fit into Agassi’s approach to raising their children?

What does Agassi’s quote tell us about his idea of parenthood?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Andre Agassi’s words, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” offer a deeply personal look at how becoming a parent changed the tennis legend’s view of his own life. Agassi grew up in a world where tennis was not simply a sport but a major part of his everyday life, with intense training and expectations starting at a very young age. Years later, after becoming one of tennis’ biggest stars, he and his wife, fellow tennis legend Steffi Graf, built a family life around their two children, Jaden and Jaz. For Agassi, watching his children grow gave him the chance to experience some of the simple moments of childhood that he felt he had missed himself.The quote is closely connected to Agassi’s own experience growing up. He started playing tennis as a young child and was pushed toward the sport by his father, Mike Agassi. His father had a clear dream for him: he wanted his son to become one of the best tennis players in the world.That dream eventually came true.Agassi went on to become world No. 1 and won eight Grand Slam singles titles during his career. But reaching that level meant spending much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis.For a young child, that kind of life can leave little room for ordinary experiences. Instead of having complete freedom to decide how he wanted to spend his time, Agassi’s days were largely connected to tennis.That is where his famous quote becomes especially powerful.When he says he “gave up” his childhood, he is looking back at the years he spent becoming a professional athlete. But he is also talking about what those sacrifices eventually allowed him to do.His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family. It allowed him to be present as his children grew up.In other words, Agassi may have missed parts of his own childhood, but later he had the opportunity to sit beside his children and watch them experience theirs. For him, that became a kind of second chance.Fatherhood gave Agassi a different way of looking at his past. When he watched Jaden and Jaz grow up, he could see the small moments of childhood from a parent’s point of view.He could watch them discover what they liked, make their own choices and develop personalities separate from their famous parents.Those moments were very different from the childhood Agassi had experienced.His early years were strongly connected to the tennis court. His father believed that constant practice and discipline were necessary if Andre Agassi was going to become a champion. That approach helped produce an incredible tennis career, but it also meant that Agassi’s childhood was far from ordinary.As a father, he wanted something different for his children.Instead of seeing childhood as preparation for a future career, Agassi wanted Jaden and Jaz to enjoy the years they were living through.That is one of the most important ideas behind his quote. He was not simply saying that he wanted to give his children more material things or better opportunities. He wanted to give them time.Time to grow.Time to explore.Time to make mistakes.Time to decide what they wanted for themselves.This became especially important because Agassi knew from personal experience how powerful parental expectations can be. He had spent years trying to become the player his father wanted him to be. As a parent, he had the chance to make sure his own children did not feel that same pressure.Steffi Graf’s role in the family’s story is important because she understood Agassi’s world better than almost anyone. Like her husband, Graf was introduced to tennis at a very young age and went on to become one of the greatest players in the history of the sport.Steffi Graf won 22 Grand Slam singles titles and spent years at the top of women’s tennis before retiring in 1999. Agassi and Graf later married and raised their two children, Jaden and Jaz.Together, they had something unusual in common: both parents knew exactly what it took to become a tennis champion, but they also knew the pressure that came with that journey.That understanding appears to have influenced the way they raised their children.Despite having two parents who were global tennis stars, Jaden and Jaz were not simply expected to follow the same path.Jaden developed a passion for baseball rather than choosing tennis as his main sport. Jaz has also been able to follow her own interests. Agassi and Graf have supported their children without making their parents’ careers the center of their lives.That is particularly meaningful when viewed alongside Agassi’s quote.The couple had already achieved what many athletes spend their entire lives chasing. They did not need their children to continue that legacy for them.Instead, they could give their children something that both parents understood the value of: choice.Agassi has also spoken warmly about Graf and the role she plays in his life. Their shared experience in professional sports gave them an understanding of the demands and sacrifices that come with elite competition.For their family, giving their children the freedom to choose their own paths became more important than creating another generation of tennis champions.At its heart, Agassi’s quote is about turning his own difficult experiences into something positive for his children.He cannot go back and change the childhood he had. He cannot erase the years of training, pressure and expectations that came with becoming a tennis player.But he can choose what kind of childhood his own children experience.That is what makes the quote about much more than tennis.Many parents work hard because they want their children to have opportunities they did not have themselves. Agassi’s story takes that idea one step further. His goal was not simply to provide his children with a comfortable life. He wanted to be present for the experiences that make childhood special.His words also show that parenthood can change the way people understand their own past.The same childhood that once felt difficult to Agassi became part of what helped him understand his children better. His experiences taught him what pressure can feel like, which may have made him more aware of the importance of giving his own children freedom.And Steffi Graf was there beside him, bringing her own experience as a former champion and a parent.Together, Agassi and Graf chose not to make their children’s lives about living up to their parents’ names. They allowed Jaden and Jaz to build identities of their own.That may be the most powerful part of Agassi’s words.He spent his childhood becoming a tennis champion. But when he became a father, he did not want his children to spend their childhood becoming something for him.He wanted to watch them simply be children.So, when Agassi says, “I gave up my childhood to be able to have my children’s childhood,” he is not only talking about sacrifice. He is talking about perspective, presence and love.He gave years of his life to tennis. Those years helped him become a champion and eventually gave him the freedom to step back and focus on his family.For Agassi, one of the greatest rewards was not another trophy or achievement. It was being able to watch his children grow up on their own terms, with Graf by his side.That is what makes his quote so relatable. Parenthood does not allow us to rewrite our own childhoods, but it can give us the chance to create a different childhood for the next generation.
Article Summary: Andre agassi’s famous quote is closely connected to his own experience growing up. Agassi spent much of his childhood training, competing and preparing for professional tennis. His success gave him the freedom to step away from tennis and spend more time with his family.

Article Title: Luka Doncic could finally get highest NBA individual award as he begins Lakers journey as a leader following Lebron James’ departure: "I think it's pretty well set up”
Article Text:
Luka Doncic. Image via: Luke Hales/ Getty Images

NBA insider predicts Luka Doncic could earn MVP award in 2026-27 season

Doncic's scoring numbers adds to the MVP push

Health and history are the final pieces of the puzzle

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Luka Doncic has spent years building an MVP resume without the hardware to show for it. That could change fast.With LeBron James gone and the Lakers now fully his team, Doncic walks into the 2026-27 season as the lone face of a franchise reshaping its identity around him. ESPN insider Tim MacMahon thinks the timing could not line up better for a first MVP trophy, and the numbers already back that theory up.MacMahon pointed out that the pressure on the Lakers is about as light as it has been since LeBron first arrived, which oddly works in Doncic's favor. Voters tend to reward players who outperform modest team expectations, and Doncic has the individual numbers to make that happen regardless of what the roster around him looks like.Last season, he averaged 33.5 points, 8.3 assists and 7.7 rebounds across 64 games as the Lakers finished 53-29. Even with those numbers, he finished fourth in MVP voting. MacMahon believes matching that production while keeping LA competitive changes the math entirely."I think it's pretty well set up for Luka to potentially win his first," MacMahon said, adding that a similar 53-win season paired with those kinds of stats would give Doncic what he called a serious case."And a narrative where the expectations for the Lakers are as low as they've been since LeBron arrived."MVP isn't the only trophy in play. ESPN's Brian Windhorst joined MacMahon on The Hoop Collective Podcast to back Doncic as an early favorite for the scoring title too. He led the league at 33.5 points per game last season, marking the second time in three years he's topped the NBA in scoring, after averaging 33.9 points with Dallas in 2024-25.Stacking a scoring title on top of MVP buzz only strengthens the individual narrative. Doncic isn't just filling a stat sheet, he's doing it while carrying more organizational weight than at any point in his career.The Lakers haven't had an MVP winner since Kobe Bryant took it home in 2007-08, and that drought hangs over this whole conversation. Doncic spent his offseason rehabbing a hamstring issue rather than chasing headlines, and he now enters camp fully healthy alongside Austin Reaves as the team's other veteran leader.Doncic has been this close before, finishing third in MVP voting back in 2023-24. What's different now is the setup around him. Stay on the floor, keep producing at his usual level, and push the Lakers past 50 wins again, and voters may finally run out of reasons to look elsewhere. Now, by all means, Doncic has to be healthy.

Article Title: Players at the US Open in New York are complaining that the smell of marijuana is becoming an unwanted distraction
Article Text:
Players at the US Open in New York say marijuana smoke is becoming an unexpected distraction/ Photo by Dave Dellinger/USTA

Boulter: ‘You don't need distractions’

Jones remembers the smell from last year's US Open

It has been an issue at the US Open before

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The 2026 US Open is set to begin on Sunday, but as the world's best players prepare for the year's final Grand Slam, some competitors are dealing with an unexpected distraction around Flushing Meadows: the smell of cannabis drifting in from a nearby park.British players Katie Boulter, Fran Jones and Harriet Dart have all noticed the smell around the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, with Boulter saying it can affect her concentration during practice and matches.The tournament begins on Aug. 30, with Carlos Alcaraz returning to individual competition for the first time since suffering a wrist injury at the Barcelona Open in April. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner will miss the event with a knee injury, while Novak Djokovic will pursue a record 25th Grand Slam title. Rising star Alex Eala is also expected to receive strong support from New York fans, while Aryna Sabalenka will look to rediscover her best form.Cannabis is legal for adults aged 21 and over in New York, although smoking is not permitted on the grounds of the tennis center. However, the venue sits beside Corona Park, and the smell can carry across to some practice and outside courts.Boulter, Britain's No. 1 and ranked 60th in the world, said she has encountered it both while practising and during matches.“Yeah, I have experienced it. You go down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot,” Boulter said.“But yeah, I'm not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on some of the specific courts.“I've played on one before and I did smell it during my match. It's something that I wouldn't like to smell in the middle of my match.“I'm trying to focus and then obviously, it takes you out of the moment and you really don't want to. You don't need distractions. So yeah, I wasn't a huge fan of it.”Boulter is not the only British player to have noticed it. Fran Jones, Britain's No. 3, recalled encountering the smell during her first-round match at last year's tournament and said she initially wondered whether it was simply part of playing so close to the park.“Last year I made a joke about that, in my first round, and I said to the guy, 'is this normal?' Because I was on the stadium, and it's next to the park,” Jones said.“He's like, 'yeah.' and I was like, 'well, no wonder I'm playing pretty well.'“This year I'll be like 'no, lock in, lock in!'”Jones, who qualified for this year's tournament, begins her campaign against Poland's Magda Linette on Monday.Harriet Dart, who also came through qualifying, took a more typically New York approach to the situation.“I mean it's New York. It's New York. I feel like everywhere you walk around, it's everywhere, no? It is what it is. Same for everyone,” Dart said.Dart will face American Peyton Stearns in the first round.The smell of cannabis has become a recurring talking point at Flushing Meadows, with players from outside Britain raising similar concerns in previous editions.In 2022, Australian doubles player Nick Kyrgios complained that a spectator smoking courtside was affecting his asthma, prompting the umpire to ask fans to refrain from smoking.A year later, Greece's Maria Sakkari pointed out the smell to the umpire during a match. She later clarified that it was not an excuse for her defeat.Novak Djokovic and Alexander Zverev have also previously noticed the smell around the tournament.The United States Tennis Association, which organises the US Open, has acknowledged the difficulty of dealing with activity taking place beyond the tournament grounds.“While we can't control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this,” the USTA said in a statement.The organisation has said it works with local police and the parks department to address smoking around the boundary of the site.With the 2026 US Open getting under way on Sunday, the cannabis smell is likely to remain a background issue at a tournament already filled with major storylines. Alcaraz will return to action, Sinner will be absent, Djokovic will chase another historic title, Eala will look to make the most of strong local support and Sabalenka will aim to regain her winning form.Boulter will open against American wildcard Carol Young Suh Lee, while Jones and Dart begin their campaigns against Linette and Stearns respectively.
Article Summary: Players at the us open in new york say marijuana smoke is becoming an unexpected distraction. Katie boulter, fran jones and harriet dart have all noticed the smell around the usta billie jean king national tennis center. The 2026 us open is set to begin on sunday.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El rubius was eliminated from mrbeast's $1 million challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: Royal challengers bengaluru (rcb) beat chennai super kings (csk) in ipl 2026 encounter at the m chinnaswamy stadium on sunday. Rcb register their second win over csk in the ipl. Tim david, rajat patidar and devdutt padikkal all scored half-centuries for rcb. Bhuvneshwar kumar took 3-41 to help rcb reach 250/3.

Article Title: Streamer DDG claims 10-year-olds sent him ‘death threats’ after controversial GTA 6 comments about younger players
Article Text:
Streamer DDG claims 10-year-olds sent him ‘death threats’ after controversial GTA 6 comments about younger players

DDG says younger GTA 6 fans missed the old games

Rockstar Games shows more of GTA 6 ahead of November release

Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look

Rapper and streamer Darryl Dwayne “DDG” Granberry Jr. has sparked a debate over who GTA 6 is really made for. During a recent livestream, DDG argued that younger players cannot fully understand the excitement around Rockstar Games’ next Grand Theft Auto title because they did not grow up playing its older games. He pointed to the long wait between GTA 5 and GTA 6 and said longtime fans had experienced the series when its graphics were much less advanced. His comments later led him to claim that he was receiving death threats from young Instagram users.DDG brought up his own experience with the series while discussing the excitement around GTA 6. He noted that GTA 5 arrived when he was 15 and said he is now 30.The rapper then argued that younger fans did not have the same experience with the franchise as older players who had followed it for years.DDG said:“GTA 5 came out when I was 15. N**** I'm 30 now. This game ain't for you young n****. That's what I'm trying to get through y'all fn**** that keep saying, 'GTA 6, GTA 6,' this is for the old n****. We waited for this sh***. We waited 15 years.”He continued by pointing to older games such as GTA: Vice City and argued that younger players never had to experience the less advanced graphics of earlier titles.The comments drew attention online, and DDG later claimed that some young users had taken their reaction too far. In a post on X, he wrote that he was receiving “death threats from 10-year-olds” on Instagram.DDG’s comments came just as Rockstar Games gave fans a much longer look at GTA 6. The studio releasedon August 27, first on Netflix and later on YouTube. Rockstar said the footage was captured entirely from the PlayStation 5.The extended look focuses on the game’s two main characters, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Their story follows the pair as they become caught in a criminal conspiracy across Leonida, the fictional state that includes Vice City. Rockstar describes their relationship as central to the game as they are forced to depend on each other after a planned job goes wrong.The footage also gives players a closer look at Leonida’s different locations, along with shoot-outs, driving sequences and character switching. Jason and Lucia can be controlled at different points, giving players two perspectives during parts of the story.

He argued that younger fans missed the old games because they did not grow up playing its older games. His comments later led him to claim that he was receiving death threats from young instagram users.

Article Text:

The 7th PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship shattered records with over 8,200 young talent nationwide, earning global recognition and fostering a culture of resilience and determination in aspiring badminton starsIn a spectacular display of badminton prowess and youthful enthusiasm, the 7th edition of the PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship (JBC) etched its name in the annals of sporting history. Celebrating a staggering participation of 8257 young champions from across India, the championship not only broke its own record set in 2022 but also clinched the title of the ‘Most kids participating in a Badminton Championship in multiple cities’ as recognised by the World Record Certification Agency (WRCA).The grand finale unfolded at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi, where the air was thick with competition, camaraderie, and the unmistakable passion for badminton. The event, graced by chief guests Chirag Shetty and Satwik Rankireddy, Asian Games Gold Medalists and JBC 2023 mentors, was a true celebration of the sport’s rising stars.The 10-city extravaganza, spanning the length and breadth of the country, showcased the unwavering commitment of PNB MetLife in nurturing young talents in the badminton arena. With participants exceeding 8200, it’s evident that the PNB MetLife JBC has become a beacon for aspiring shuttlers, highlighting the deep-seated passion for badminton among the diverse and talented youth of India.Beyond the glitz and glamour of the record-breaking numbers, the championship holds a special place in the hearts of those at the helm. Ashish Kumar Srivastava, MD and CEO of PNB MetLife, expressed pride in not just surpassing their own world record but also in contributing to India’s glory on the international badminton stage. The championship, he emphasized, is not merely a competition but a significant milestone in creating a pan-India badminton ecosystem.This edition of the JBC saw a strategic partnership with world champions Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, who served as mentors for the young talents. Sameer Bansal, Chief Distribution Officer of PNB MetLife, acknowledged the pivotal role played by these champions in inspiring the next generation of badminton stars. The focus, according to Bansal, is on unleashing the latent potential of young shuttlers and preparing them for global excellence.The Delhi chapter of the championship witnessed some nail-biting action with over 1000 participants competing fiercely across various categories. From Ananya Talyan’s stellar performance in Girls Singles Under 9 to Divyansh Rawat’s triumph in Boys Singles Under 17, the young talents left no shuttle unturned in their quest for victory.The results from the Delhi leg not only showcased the raw talent but also highlighted the championship’s commitment to breaking barriers. The PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship is not just about records; it’s about fostering a culture of healthy living, determination, and resilience among the future champions of the sport.In the words of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy, the championship serves as an invaluable platform.---------------------------------------------------------------As we celebrate the successful culmination of the 7th edition of PNB MetLife Junior Badminton Championship , we take pride in surpassing our own world record for highest participation and for being recognized by World Record Certification Agency. Beyond the records, JBC represents a significant milestone in our mission to lay the groundwork for India’ s glory and success on the international badminton stage by creating a pan-India badminton ecosystem that nurtures champions at the grassroots levelThis year has been especially remarkable for PNB MetLife JBC as we joined hands with world champions Chirag Shetty and Satwiksairaj Rankireddy as JBC Mentors for the young talents associated with this tournament. They have played a pivotal role in inspiring young shuttlers to dream big and elevate their game and skills. We are eager for the next edition to unfold in our journey of unveiling the latent badminton potential across our nation and preparing them for global excellenceIt’s inspiring to witness the boundless talent and enthusiasm within our young athletes. My journey as JBC mentor has been incredibly fulfilling, as I got the opportunity to guide these budding champions and witness the journey of these young badminton stars. This championship is more than a competition; it is a platform that nurtures dreams, ignites aspirations, and, I believe, it is laying the foundation for future gold medalists in the makingTournaments like these serve as an invaluable platform for nurturing and harnessing the potential of our country’s young badminton stars. Witnessing the enthusiasm, passion, and skill displayed by these emerging shuttlers reinforces the belief that our country has an immense reservoir of talent. My association as a JBC mentor has been a source of immense pride, particularly given the role that the championship is playing in creating an incredible platform that is serving as a powerful catalyst, empowering young players and bolstering their confidence to become future champions

It is reliably learnt that both Pandya and Reddy have been training intensely at the BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) and operating at full capacity as they prepare to return to international cricket.As for Washington Sundar, he spent the weekend in Chennai and will report back to the CoE this week to prove his fitness before selection. The 32-year-old has been training at the CoE. While the Afghanistan T20Is could be touch-and-go, the Asian Games shouldn't face any availability issues if there are no late hiccups during his rehabilitation."Bumrah is progressing well. He is being closely monitored and while the Afghanistan T20Is could be too close for comfort, the Asian Games seem highly likely, provided there are no late surprises," explains the source.After the recent outings in Ireland and England, the Indian team management is exploring options of left-arm spinners in the shortest format. Article Title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scripts history, breaks all-time Duleep Trophy record in semi-final

Youngest to hit Duleep Trophy fifty

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has added another record to his rapidly growing list of achievements, becoming the youngest batter in Duleep Trophy history to score a half-century.The 15-year-old achieved the feat during East Zone’s Duleep Trophy 2026 semi-final against Central Zone in Bengaluru, reaching his fifty in just 42 balls with a six.Sooryavanshi eventually finished with an impressive 92 off 81 balls, falling just eight runs short of a century. His knock included aggressive strokeplay and came at a crucial stage for East Zone.At 15 years and 175 days, Sooryavanshi surpassed a record that had stood for 57 years. The previous youngest batter to score a Duleep Trophy fifty was Laxman Singh, who was 16 years and 23 days old when he achieved the feat in 1969.He has now moved ahead of Laxman Singh and Piyush Chawla, who was 16 years and 307 days old when he scored a Duleep Trophy fifty in 2025.Sooryavanshi’s batting milestone came after he had already found himself in an unusual leadership role earlier in the match.On Day 1, East Zone captain Ishan Kishan was forced off the field during the morning session after being struck on his right wrist. Sooryavanshi stepped in as stand-in captain for around an hour on either side of lunch before Kishan returned to take charge.During his brief spell as captain, Sooryavanshi also made an important intervention with the DRS.In the 40th over, Central Zone opener and wicketkeeper Aryan Juyal was on 46 when he poked at a delivery from Mukesh Kumar outside off. East Zone appealed for a caught-behind dismissal, but the on-field umpire turned it down.Sooryavanshi backed his judgement and opted for a review. UltraEdge showed a small spike as the ball passed the bat, confirming the edge and giving East Zone a crucial wicket.Earlier, East Zone made an excellent start after Kishan won the toss and chose to field.Mukesh Kumar and Abhijit Sarkar picked up three wickets apiece, while Mohammed Shami and off-spinner Md Kounain Quraishi claimed two each as Central Zone were bowled out for 266 in 80.1 overs.Rinku Singh top-scored with 60 off 88 balls, while Juyal contributed 46. Rinku also put together a 55-run sixth-wicket partnership with Harsh Dubey, who scored 27, after Central Zone slipped to 125/5.Quraishi broke that stand by trapping Dubey lbw in the 60th over, triggering another collapse. Saransh Jain made 13 and Aryan Pandey scored 22, while Yash Thakur provided late impetus with a quick 30 off 26 balls.Central Zone were eventually bowled out for 266, giving East Zone the platform to take control of the semi-final.For Sooryavanshi, the semi-final has already been a memorable one. On the opening day, he briefly took over as East Zone captain after Ishan Kishan left the field, and a day later he produced another record-breaking performance. Sooryavanshi brought up his half-century in just 42 balls before going on to score 92 off 81 deliveries.The only disappointment was that the teenage star could not complete another century, falling just eight runs short of three figures.
Article Summary: Vaibhav sooryavanshi is the youngest batter in duleep trophy history to score a half-century. The 15-year-old achieved the feat during east zone’s semi-final against central zone in bengaluru. He reached his fifty in just 42 balls with a six, falling just eight runs short of a century.

Article Title: IPL media rights: Does the BCCI have a Plan B?
Article Text:
IPL Trophy (Photo Credit: BCCI/IPL)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Indian cricket board's reluctance to seek better price discovery ahead of the upcoming IPL and home bilateral media rights tender is weighing heavily on the industry.With about six months to go before the final IPL edition of the 2023-27 rights cycle begins, there is growing concern among cricket's biggest stakeholders that the absence of a credible bidder other than JioStar will prevent an accurate assessment of the property's value, and, in turn, deny the market the competitive tension that has driven IPL rights upwards for a decade.That sentiment was echoed by none other than Uday Shankar, the media entrepreneur who serves as vice-chairman of JioStar, at the recent ET World Leaders Forum."Ten years ago, you would have multiple and serious media companies (around four) competing for major sports rights. You'd have four or more companies genuinely fighting for properties. Today, increasingly, it feels as if we are the only ones standing. And that's not healthy," Shankar said."The fundamental issue is that the cost of the rights has risen dramatically. But the ability to monetise those rights hasn't necessarily risen at the same rate. The value of sports is enormous, but the rights holder, broadcaster and platform all need to participate in a sustainable ecosystem," he added.The worrying part of this narrative is the absence of a Plan B for Indian cricket. That JioStar will bid healthily for the IPL is a given: its subscription numbers are heavily leveraged against cricket consumption.What is baffling is the BCCI's inability to bring more participants to the table.Players such as YouTube and Netflix have been engaging aggressively with sport in the West. YouTube's move into rights aggregation and bundling has, in fact, become an industry trend of its own.YouTube increasingly treats sport not as a series of standalone rights acquisitions but as the anchor of a broader pay-TV and subscription ecosystem. Its seven-year deal for exclusive US distribution of NFL Sunday Ticket — worth a reported $2 billion a season — works both as a value-add for YouTube TV subscribers and as a standalone product sold through YouTube channels.Average revenue per user in the West bears little resemblance to what the subcontinent generates, which complicates the assumption that volume alone wins the argument. Even so, Indian cricket remains the only market in this part of the world worth a player like YouTube testing the waters in.More recently, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos told The Economic Times that the streaming giant was interested in live sport, including cricket, but had no intention of becoming a "conventional full-season sports broadcaster".If so, a property like the IPL sits squarely in Netflix's territory. The storytelling potential of an India-first sports property speaks to a billion-plus domestic audience, a vast global diaspora, and to markets where cricket remains one of India's most effective exports and a quiet instrument of soft power."At some point, the economics have to make sense," Shankar says. For that to happen, the responsibility must lie with the federation itself to market what is, by any measure, a high-value product.The IPL may be India's most prized prime-time asset. But to assume that a media player several time zones away is fully clued in to the India story, without hearing it first-hand from the people writing it, is optimistic at best.Which is why it matters that the BCCI arrives at this tender with a genuine marketing strategy: one that puts the IPL in front of the dozens of media, technology and streaming platforms worldwide that could plausibly be interested.JioStar is the BCCI's Plan A. The question is whether there is a Plan B, or a Plan C.
Article Summary: The indian cricket board's reluctance to seek better price discovery ahead of the upcoming ipl and home bilateral media rights tender is weighing heavily on the industry. There is growing concern among cricket's biggest stakeholders that the absence of a credible bidder other than jiostar will prevent an accurate assessment of the property's value.

Article Title: 'Praggnanandhaa is No. 1 in the world': Viswanathan Anand after India's first Grand Chess Tour title | Exclusive
Article Text:
R Praggnanandhaa and Viswanathan Anand

A family photo after Vaishali's Women's Candidates win (Tushar Damor/ChessBase India)

I think at the moment, I would say he (Pragg) is the number one player in the world. Viswanathan Anand, former five-time World Chess Champion

R Praggnanandhaa (Photo by Lennart Ootes)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: You remember the photo that made rounds on social media last April, just after Vaishali Rameshbabu, Praggnanandhaa's elder sister, had landed at the Chennai airport with the Women's Candidates medal wrapped around her neck. It was a photo of her family.Praggnanandhaa was there too, his facial gesture mirroring anything but the sorrow of an underwhelming campaign in the open category of the Candidates, his hand holding a placard congratulating his sister on her homecoming.If that was Vaishali's moment, Praggnanandhaa's is now.Late Thursday in St Louis, he beat Fabiano Caruana 15-13 to win the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Finals, becoming the first Indian and only the seventh player in the tournament's 11-year history to do it The prize money was $200,000. But even more than the prize money, it is about a 21-year-old who somewhat imploded at the 2026 Candidates and now sits, by one of the sport's most respected judges, at the top of the world.During an interaction with TimesofIndia.com, Viswanathan Anand , who is set to return to the board with Alaskan Knights for the new season of the Global Chess League (GCL) this September, assessed Praggnanandhaa's turnaround since that Candidates low."During the Candidates, he was having a kind of slump," the former five-time World Chess Champion said. "His play had already started to decline at the end of last year, compared to the first half, but in the Candidates, it was really not very impressive.And then I thought he must have been a bit gloomy."What followed, in Anand's telling, was something closer to a pattern than a one-off recovery."In Norway Chess, he was not doing well. At some point, there were four rounds left, and he was in the bottom. And then he won four games in a row," Anand explained. "He did something similar here, though his performance was much better in Grand Chess Tour and also in the Rapid. He won the Rapid, did well enough in the Blitz to win the tournament. Then he was sort of competing for first place here."It's the shape of these comebacks that Anand keeps returning to. "He has this capacity, and it's becoming more and more noticeable that he's able to win late games and change everything," he remarked. "And that's a very, very rare skill and useful skill to have."Then came the line that will follow Praggnanandhaa into the Olympiad next month. "I think at the moment, I would say he's the number one player in the world," Anand told this website with utmost authority."Well, Magnus doesn't compete in the same events, but nonetheless, you know, if you take classical included, and I know Pragg, in the tournaments which happened in August and all, he performed incredibly well. If you go back to Norway Chess and then see the development from there, I think it's just fantastic."It's not an idle comparison. Praggnanandhaa's road to St Louis ran through 27 rapid and blitz games, nine classical games, and 16 more across the semifinals and final. He arrived having already beaten Magnus Carlsen twice in classical chess in Norway earlier this year, including a stretch of four straight classical wins to close out Oslo.In the GCT final itself, he lost the opening classical game to Caruana and fumbled a likely equaliser in the second before finding his footing, winning both rapid games to seize control, then holding the four-game blitz section to a 4-4 draw to close it out.He'd already avenged a bruising from World Championship Challenger Javokhir Sindarov, who beat him twice at the Cyprus Candidates, by finishing joint-first with him at the Sinquefield Cup.ALSO READ: Praggnanandhaa’s invisible second: The making of Vaibhav Suri He'd been beaten there by Vincent Keymer, too, before eliminating the German in the GCT semifinal.For a player whose technical range and universal style have long had experts rating him the most complete of India's young elite, the Candidates collapse had looked like the one gap in the resume. St Louis just closed it, in front of the one man whose word on the subject still carries the most weight in Indian chess.
Article Summary: Praggnanandhaa beat fabiano caruana 15-13 to win the grand chess tour (gct) finals. The 21-year-old is the first indian and only the seventh player in the tournament's 11-year history to do it. Viswanathan anand: "i think at the moment, i would say he's the number one players in the world" he arrived having already beaten magnus carlsen twice in classical chess in norway earlier this year.

Article Title: ‘Social media player’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer brutally tears into Babar Azam after Lord’s horror show
Article Text:
Babar Azam (ANI Photo)

Basit questions Babar’s Test record

Saud Shakeel also comes under fire

Pakistan’s batting collapses again

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan batter Basit Ali has launched a strong criticism of Babar Azam after the Pakistan captain endured another disappointing outing in the second Test against England at Lord’s.Pakistan suffered a 194-run defeat on Sunday to concede the three-match series 2-0, with their batting once again failing to withstand pressure. Chasing 389 in the fourth innings, Pakistan were bowled out for 194, while Babar managed only six after scoring eight in the first innings.For Basit, Babar’s latest failure raised a much bigger question about his contribution when Pakistan need him most.Speaking on The Game Plan show, Basit compared Babar with several legendary Pakistan batters, arguing that the country’s greatest players established their reputations by delivering in difficult situations.“They didn't become great players just like that. I'm not even talking about Sachin Tendulkar. I'm talking about my own countrymen".Basit then questioned whether Babar has done enough when Pakistan have been under pressure.“When you don't do anything in difficult times, what's the point? You're a great player in your fan following. You're a great player in front of social media.”The former batter then directly turned his attention to Babar and highlighted his long wait for a Test century.Babar’s last Test hundred came in December 2022, when he scored 161 against New Zealand in Karachi. Since then, he has been unable to reach three figures in the format.“When will you do it? I'm talking about Babar [Azam]. I'll take his name. He hasn't scored a [Test] hundred in four years. When will you do it?” Basit said.He also expressed his frustration at Babar’s dismissal at Lord’s, particularly because Pakistan’s batting heavily relied on their captain to provide a substantial contribution.“It's a matter of pain. When the entire country's batting depends on you. At least don't get out by hitting such a shot,” Basit lamented.Babar’s dismissal came early in the chase when he got into trouble against Jofra Archer. The Pakistan captain attempted to leave a short delivery but ended up offering a simple catch to Jordan Cox in the slip cordon.Basit did not spare the other Pakistan batters either. Saud Shakeel provided the strongest resistance during the chase, scoring 97 off 132 balls and helping Pakistan recover after they slipped to 14/3. However, his attempt to accelerate towards a century ultimately cost him his wicket.After smashing two sixes in an over from Josh Tongue, Shakeel fell three runs short of his hundred while attempting another aggressive shot.“I'm not even satisfied with Saud [Shakeel]'s shot. You've taken on five fielders and you're hitting such a shot,” Basit complained.Mohammad Rizwan was another target of Basit’s criticism after the wicketkeeper-batter scored only one before being dismissed lbw by Ollie Robinson.“What shot did [Mohammad] Rizwan hit? Doesn't he have any sense? Is he playing a Test match or street cricket?” Basit said.Pakistan’s problems with the bat were evident almost immediately in their chase.Robinson dismissed Azan Awais lbw before producing a delivery that breached Abdullah Shafique’s defence and hit the off stump, leaving Pakistan in serious trouble.Archer then removed Babar, and Pakistan went into lunch with Saud Shakeel and Shan Masood attempting to rebuild.Shakeel eventually reached his fifty from 54 balls and formed a useful partnership with Masood. But Robinson returned after the rain interruption to dismiss Masood, before removing Rizwan soon afterwards.With Imam-ul-Haq unavailable to bat because of his calf injury, Pakistan’s hopes were effectively over. Shakeel continued fighting but fell on 97, with Tongue then wrapping up the tail.England’s bowlers dominated the final innings, with Robinson finishing with eight wickets in the match, as Pakistan were dismissed for 194.The defeat leaves Pakistan 2-0 down in the series, with the third and final Test to be played at Edgbaston in Birmingham from September 9.
Article Summary: Babar azam has not scored a test hundred in four years, says basit ali. The pakistan captain was dismissed for six by jofra archer at lord's. Basit also questioned the contribution of saud shakeel and mohammad rizwan. Shakeel continued fighting but fell on 97, with tongue then wrapping up the tail.

Article Title: Manchester City make shock move to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool in £85m deal: Reports
Article Text:
Manchester City have opened talks for Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo, with reports valuing the Dutchman at £85m/ Image: X

Why could Gakpo leave Liverpool?

Gakpo has been an important part of Liverpool's attack

City preparing for a busy finish to the window

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Manchester City have opened talks with Liverpool over a potential move for Cody Gakpo, with the Dutch forward emerging as one of the biggest names who could still change clubs before the transfer window closes.According to reports, City made formal contact with Liverpool on Saturday evening regarding a move for the 27-year-old. ESPN, citing its own sources, reported that discussions between the clubs had gathered pace and that Liverpool value Gakpo at £85 million ($115m).Gakpo has also attracted interest from Tottenham Hotspur, but sources cited by BBC Sport indicate that Manchester City is the forward's preferred destination should he leave Anfield.The possibility of Gakpo's departure comes at a particularly interesting point in Liverpool's transfer window. The Reds have agreed a deal to sign Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola for a fee that could rise to £123 million, according to BBC Sport, and Liverpool are understood to want another forward through the door before allowing Gakpo to leave.Liverpool have an interest in Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh and Crystal Palace forward Ismaïla Sarr, with the club having already seen bids for both players rejected, according to reports.That means Gakpo's situation is not simply a matter of whether City are prepared to meet Liverpool's valuation; the Reds also need to make sure they have sufficient attacking options before sanctioning his exit.ESPN reported that City have been encouraged by Gakpo's interest in a move to the Etihad Stadium and are pressing ahead with negotiations.Gakpo joined Liverpool from his boyhood club PSV Eindhoven in January 2023 and has since scored 33 goals in 91 Premier League appearances.The forward has also started the new season in good form. He scored in Liverpool's opening league fixture, a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United, and then provided the assist for Alexander Isak's goal in Saturday's 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest at Anfield.Gakpo started against Forest despite the growing speculation surrounding his future, with Liverpool twice having to come from behind to rescue a point.His possible departure would therefore leave Andoni Iraola with another significant attacking decision to make, particularly with Liverpool already close to bringing Barcola into the squad.Manchester City are also expected to remain active during the final days of the transfer window.According to ESPN, City have already agreed a deal with Palmeiras for Brazilian winger Allan, while Savio and Omar Marmoush have both left the club to join Tottenham this summer.The club have also been working on their midfield, having already spent more than £200 million on that area following the departures of Bernardo Silva and Rodri, with Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi among their additions.ESPN's sources say City are expected to make at least one late bid for Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernández as well as continuing discussions over Gakpo.For Liverpool, meanwhile, the decision is becoming increasingly time-sensitive, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday, September 1. The club must now weigh City's interest against its own need to maintain numbers in attack, particularly with Barcola's arrival close and further moves for Minteh or Sarr still being pursued.
Article Summary: Manchester city have opened talks with liverpool over a potential move for cody gakpo, according to reports. The dutch forward could still leave anfield before the transfer window closes on september 1. Reports claim liverpool value the 27-year-old at £85 million. Tottenham hotspur are also said to be interested in the forward.

Article Title: Michael Carrick says it is ‘lazy’ to claim Man Utd lacked passion after embarrassing 2-0 defeat to newly promoted Hull City
Article Text:
Manchester United's interim head coach Michael Carrick walks on the pitch at the end of the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester United and Nottingham Forest in Manchester, England, Sunday, May 17, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

Carrick rejects claims United lacked desire

Carrick wants United to respond

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions that Manchester United lacked passion or motivation in their shock opening-day defeat to newly promoted Hull City, calling it “lazy” to reduce the performance to a lack of effort.United began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-0 defeat at the MKM Stadium despite having 71.7% possession, with Hull scoring twice from set pieces in the first half. The result has led to criticism of United's attitude and desire, but Carrick insists there was more to the defeat than simply a failure to try.United were accused of lacking passion and intensity during the defeat, but Carrick defended his players ahead of Sunday's home meeting with another newly promoted side, Ipswich Town.“Teams lose games and win games, and it's not just because you try or you don't try,” Carrick told a news conference.“There are all sorts of different reasons.
